page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for standard enterprise workloads requiring balanced compute and memory. The instance features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores running on a 2.2 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with two threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 128.0 GB, providing an exact 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes 55 MB of L3 cache, standard AVX and AES-NI instruction support, and operates without attached local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded applications. The server attained a PassMark CPU score of 38099.23 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 42996.45, both placing within the middle 50% tier. Memory throughput remains balanced, registering 98.83 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 44.29 GB/sec write bandwidth. Operational testing reflects stable throughput for common enterprise roles, delivering 21.98 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 18.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary performance tradeoff lies in single-threaded operations. While stress-ng single-core execution reached the top 25% tier at 2685.48, Geekbench single-core performance registered in the bottom 10% with a score of 934.0. Single-threaded data compression tasks similarly registered in the lowest percentile, yielding 19.01 GB/sec in gzip compression and 7.12 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. The processor configuration lacks advanced vector features like AVX-512 and AMX, bounding dense matrix and specialized machine learning acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-32 provides dependable, high-density compute capacity without the pricing premiums of bare-metal or GPU-accelerated configurations. Its balanced ratio makes it suitable for container orchestration, multi-threaded CI/CD pipelines, web serving clusters, and intermediate relational database deployments that rely on persistent network storage rather than local NVMe hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-32 is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. It is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying on external network block volumes. In performance testing, multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth placed consistently in the middle 50% tier, achieving 21.98 million Redis SET operations per second and 18.06 GB/sec in static web serving. However, single-core benchmarks showed limitations, with Geekbench single-core scores and gzip compression falling into the bottom 10%. With support for standard instruction sets like AVX and AES, the e2-standard-32 delivers cost-effective resource density for multi-threaded enterprise services, web application tiers, CI/CD runners, and distributed container workloads.
